# Results — Study 733 (Kentucky-Derby-Effect)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **the
Kentucky Derby (the "Run for the Roses", first Saturday in May) is a market event**:
either a broad market seasonal, or a pop in the one US-listed stock that literally runs
the race, Churchill Downs Inc. (`CHDN`). Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month). Fingerprint `4b4d7494b219` (`SPY` + `CHDN`, one combined
panel, 7,166 rows, 1998-01-02 → 2026-06-30).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes: `SPY` (S&P 500 ETF, the market-seasonal proxy) + `CHDN` (Churchill Downs Inc.), one combined panel, 7,166 rows, 1998-01-02 → 2026-06-30 |
| Calendar | **hardcoded**: 26 Kentucky Derbys 2000→2025, each a first-Saturday-in-May Saturday except **2020** (postponed by COVID-19 to 5 September, run not cancelled) — Wikipedia "Kentucky Derby" / "List of Kentucky Derby winners" |
| Two legs | **CHDN** (the gambling name, abnormal = CHDN window return − SPY, a β=1 market model) on all **26** events; **market** (the SPY seasonal, drift-removed constant-mean model) on the **25** first-Saturday-in-May events (2020's September running dropped — not a May observation, flagged not hidden) |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* of the windowed abnormal return across independent, non-overlapping yearly events (the correct unit — not a daily panel); Wilson hit-rate interval; a 20-seed × 200-draw random-window placebo per cut (the drift-neutral primary test for the market leg); Welch *t* for the "CHDN vs seasonal" third axis |
| Execution / costs | one documented convention: the Derby runs **Saturday** (non-trading), so **day(-1)** = last close before the race (does not know the result), **day(0)** = first close after (fully public). Signal windows run day(-1)→day(-1)+k; the **run-up** (day(-6)→day(-1)) is *calendar-known* and tradable with no result look-ahead; the **capture** enters day(0), net of 2× one-way cost × NAV (`COST_BPS = 10` for a mid-cap single stock, wider than an ETF) |
| Survivorship / exposure | **CHDN has full tape coverage** back to 1998 — no survivorship funnel (unlike 708). The named caveat is **exposure dilution**: CHDN in 2000 was a near-pure racetrack operator; CHDN today is a diversified gaming company (regional casinos, TwinSpires online wagering, historical-racing machines) for which the Derby is a shrinking slice of revenue — the direct exposure the folklore assumes has *faded* over exactly the window tested |

## The gambling name — CHDN abnormal return vs SPY (β=1 market model)

| window | n | mean AR | *t* | hit rate (Wilson 95%) | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| run-up, day(-6)→day(-1) | 26 | +0.359% | +0.55 | 13/26 = 50.0% [32.1%, 67.9%] | 0.406 |
| 1 week, day(-1)→day(+5) | 26 | −0.063% | −0.06 | 11/26 = 42.3% [25.5%, 61.1%] | — |
| 1 month, day(-1)→day(+21) | 26 | −0.195% | −0.17 | 13/26 = 50.0% [32.1%, 67.9%] | 0.691 |

The stock that literally runs the Derby does **nothing** distinguishable around its own
marquee event, at any horizon. Every |*t*| ≤ 0.55; every hit rate straddles 50%; the
mild positive run-up drift (+0.36%) sits deep in the middle of its own random-window
placebo (*p* = 0.41). This is the cleanest possible null: the most-exposed instrument,
full tape coverage, and no signal.

## The market seasonal — SPY window return, drift removed (constant-mean model)

| window | n | mean AR | *t* | hit rate (Wilson 95%) | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| run-up, day(-6)→day(-1) | 25 | +0.003% | +0.01 | 12/25 = 48.0% [30.0%, 66.5%] | — |
| **1 week, day(-1)→day(+5)** | 25 | **−0.617%** | **−1.43** | 7/25 = 28.0% [14.3%, 47.6%] | **0.107** (left) |
| 1 month, day(-1)→day(+21) | 25 | −0.319% | −0.41 | 16/25 = 64.0% [44.5%, 79.8%] | 0.368 (left) |

The single sub-noise whisper in the whole study is a **week-after dip**: in the trading
week following the first Saturday in May, the S&P underperforms its own average by
−0.62% (naive one-sample *t* = −1.43, hit rate a low 7/25). This is the folkloric "Sell
in May" boundary showing up — but it does **not** clear the desk's bar even raw, and the
drift-neutral random-window placebo puts it firmly inside the luck cloud (*p* = 0.11): a
random same-length window on the same tape produces a dip this deep about one time in
nine.

## Tradability — the costed "trade it" timer (the naive-stat trap)

Enter at day(0)'s close (first public price after the Saturday race), net of 2× one-way
cost × NAV.

| leg / window | gross | net @ 10 bps (*t*) | net @ 5 bps (*t*) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| CHDN run-up (calendar-known) | +0.359% | +0.159% (+0.25) | +0.259% (+0.40) |
| CHDN, 1 week | +0.197% | −0.003% (−0.00) | +0.097% (+0.10) |
| CHDN, 1 month | +0.109% | −0.091% (−0.08) | +0.009% (+0.01) |
| **market, 1 week** | −0.602% (*t* = −1.58) | **−0.802% (−2.11)** | −0.702% (−1.85) |
| market, 1 month | −0.300% | −0.500% (−0.65) | −0.400% (−0.52) |

The one cut whose *t*-stat **crosses the |t| ≥ 2 line is a mirage of the arithmetic**:
the market/1-week seasonal is already −0.60% gross; *subtracting* a round trip of costs
makes the number *more* negative (−0.80%) and its *t* *more* extreme (−2.11) — costs
inflating an apparent "short-the-Derby-week" edge rather than eroding it. That is exactly
backwards from a real tradable signal. Its own left-tail placebo (**p = 0.111**) says the
move is unremarkable, and executing it means **shorting the S&P** for one week, 25 times,
paying spread *and* borrow to harvest a dip that is inside the noise. Nothing here is
bankable.

## Robustness — jackknife on the market/1-week dip

Leave-one-out on the 25 market/1-week events: full-sample *t* = **−1.43**; the jackknife
range is **[−2.42, −0.999]** — drop the single worst year and it "clears" −2, keep it and
it does not. A number that swings across the certification line depending on which one of
25 years you exclude is fragile by definition, and it never had placebo support to begin
with.

## Event anatomy — mean cumulative abnormal return by trading-day offset

Re-anchored so the run-up start (offset −5) = 0; offset 0 = day(-1), the last pre-race
close.

| offset | −5 | −3 | −1 | 0 | +1 | +3 | +5 | +10 | +15 | +21 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| CHDN | 0.000% | +0.778% | +0.621% | +0.249% | −0.016% | −0.305% | +0.186% | −0.241% | +0.092% | +0.053% |
| market | 0.000% | −0.127% | −0.353% | −0.020% | −0.034% | −0.384% | −0.638% | −0.365% | −0.747% | −0.339% |

CHDN wanders up a touch into the race and gives it all back — a flat, directionless path,
not an event reaction. The market path drifts gently *down* across the window (the "Sell
in May" texture), bottoming near −0.75% around day +15, but every point on it is well
within one placebo standard deviation of zero.

## Third axis — "Sell in May?" (does the Derby mark a market turn?) & CHDN vs seasonal

The Derby sits on the first Saturday in May, the folkloric start of the weak season. The
market leg above *is* the "Sell in May" test at event resolution: a directional dip that
fails its placebo (*p* = 0.11–0.37) and its jackknife. **Not supported.** For
completeness, the Welch *t* of CHDN's abnormal return minus the market seasonal's (May
years only) is +0.58 (1 week) / +0.10 (1 month) — CHDN is trivially "better" than a
market that is drifting down, but neither is distinguishable from zero.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic paired (CHDN-like, SPY-like) log-return world (ρ ≈ 0.60, CHDN idio vol >
market) with a scheduled synthetic first-Saturday calendar and a TUNABLE planted
"Derby bump" landing on the first session after each race; no network.

| world | one-sample *t* (capture detector, k=5) |
|---|--:|
| null (bump = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.29** (sd 1.03), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** |
| planted bump = +2.0% | **+2.16** |
| planted bump = +3.0% | **+4.18** |

The detector recovers a planted post-race bump and does not fire on the null (1/20 seeds
at |t| ≥ 2, in line with the false-positive rate at n = 26). *(A faithful-engine / power
check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The most directly-exposed instrument, CHDN, is flat at every horizon
  (|*t*| ≤ 0.55, placebo *p* ≥ 0.41) with full tape coverage — the cleanest kind of null.
  The market seasonal's only sub-noise whisper is a week-after dip (−0.62%, naive
  *t* = −1.43) that misses the bar even raw and fails its drift-neutral placebo
  (*p* = 0.11). No cut clears a robust |*t*| ≥ 2 with placebo confirmation.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** No costed, zero-look-ahead cut is bankable. The only |*t*|
  that crosses 2 (market/1-week net, −2.11) is an artifact of *charging costs against an
  already-negative number*, dies under its own placebo (*p* = 0.11), and would require
  shorting the S&P 25 times to harvest a dip inside the noise.
- **"Sell in May?" — NOT SUPPORTED.** The Derby-week market dip is real in sign but inside
  the random-window luck cloud and fragile to a single year — the folklore's boundary is
  not a market turning point you could have traded.
